title: Lisa Brown as role model and starting on tenor
summary: After her father died when she was 32 she took up saxophone, inspired by seeing Lisa Brown play alto in Boston Latin bands, joined her first band, a Latin band, and took lessons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Were there role models for you, man or woman, coming up?

Yes there were. And that was a great big factor for me. What happened was that in the subsequent decade, that is when I was 32, my father died and I decided sort of the next day, if not right at the funeral, that now I’m going to also play the saxophone. And I got hold of the sax, it wasn’t his at the time, but I started practicing. But I didn’t think of joining a band until I heard, her name is Lisa Brown. She was an alto sax player who was playing around in Boston in some different Latin bands. And I went to see her. And as soon as I saw her playing it was like now I’ve seen a woman playing saxophone, now I’m going to go join a band. And then I got into my first band, which was a Latin band. And yeah, it was very important to me.
Was it a tenor you started out on?
I did. I started on tenor, yeah. I’m pretty sure I started on tenor.
